messages:
lina: ping — opened PR that tweaks how we load runtime secrets for private packs. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4726

lina: main concern: the change centralizes a small 'shared_config' file that ends up in on-prem packages. want a quick security review on whether any secret material could leak to builds or package artifacts. not ready to merge.

arun: quick skim — can you paste the diff for the loader? specifically which files get bundled into the tarball?

lina: sure. small snippet from the loader:
```
# load_shared.py
def load_shared(path):
    with open(path) as f:
        cfg = json.load(f)
    return cfg.get('secrets', {}), cfg.get('meta', {})
```
The packaging step uses `scripts/package_onprem.sh` which currently copies `shared_config.json` if present.

sam: ran a quick secret-scan locally against the branch. scanner flagged one value that looks like a base64 token in `sample_shared_config.json` (dev-only) — not present in prod, but worth removing.

security-bot: automated-scan — findings: 1 medium; file `configs/sample_shared_config.json` contains simulated token-like string. Recommend redaction before merge. (rule: base64-like 24+ chars)

maya: couple questions: 1) are we shipping any private keys or service account material in that config? 2) for private/onprem installs, do customers expect any of these configs to be pre-populated?

lina: answers: 1) no private keys — only short-lived auth tokens used by test harnesses, but they ended up in the sample file. 2) we do not auto-populate for customers; packaging previously skipped sample files but this change made the check too greedy.

arun: mitigation suggestion: ensure packaging step excludes `*sample*` and `.example` files; add an explicit allowlist for what to bundle. Also switch loader to require explicit env var to load non-prod configs: `RW_LOAD_SHARED=true`.

lina: plan: redact sample tokens, update package script to exclude samples, add env gate to loader, and add unit test that package artifact doesn't contain `shared_config.json`. I'll push a fix later today.

sam: also suggest adding an integration check that fails CI if any file matching `/sample|example/i` contains token-like strings. simple grep + base64 regex.

maya: also flagging operational change: for onprem installs we should document that customers must provide secrets via their KMS/HSM or env, not bundled. add a short note in PRIVATE_DEPLOY.md and mention rotation guidance.

lina: will update docs and add the CI scan. can I get a security approval after I push the fixes?

arun: thumbs up to that flow. i can do a follow-up review once the changes land.

maya: please also add a canary deploy tag on the Dedicated side in case packaging behavior affects rollout.

deploy-bot: merge window suggestion: tomorrow 10:00-12:00 PT — mark if you need a hold.

lina: thanks all — will push the redaction + packaging guard + CI test in a follow-up commit and ping here for explicit approvals. cc @maya @arun @sam :thumbsup:

maya: :+1: approved pending the redaction and CI test.

arun: approve after CI passes.

sam: LGTM after scanner clears the branch.
